What to expect on your invoice

We quote the full cost before any work begins. No diagnostic fee surprises, no add-ons after the fact. Here are typical ranges for common services in the DFW area.

Diagnostic / Service Call
$89 – $125

Common Repairs

Capacitor, contactor, thermostat, drain line, blower motor. Most single-component repairs fall in this range.

Refrigerant Service

Full system inspection, coil cleaning, drain flush, electrical check, and filter replacement. Per system. Book before summer for best availability.

New System Installation
$5,500 – $14,000

Complete system replacement including equipment, labor, and permits. Range depends on home size, system type, and efficiency rating.

FAQ

Common questions answered.

Can’t find your question? Call us directly at (214) 778-6461 and we’ll answer it in plain English.

Should I repair or replace my AC system?

A general rule: if the repair cost is more than half the price of a new system, and your unit is over 10 years old, replacement usually makes more financial sense. We will always give you both options with honest numbers and let you decide. We do not push replacements.

How long does a typical repair take?

Most repairs are completed the same day. We stock our trucks with the most common parts so we rarely need a second visit for standard fixes. Complex repairs like compressor replacements may require 1–2 days for parts sourcing.

Do you charge extra for weekend or after-hours calls?

For standard after-hours calls we are transparent about any additional fees upfront. For emergency situations call us directly and we will tell you the exact cost before we dispatch. No surprise charges on the invoice.

What does a tune-up actually include?

Our seasonal tune-up covers: thermostat calibration, electrical component inspection, capacitor and contactor testing, coil cleaning, condensate drain flush, refrigerant pressure check, filter replacement, and a full written system report. We do not check a box and leave — we document what we find.

My AC is blowing warm air. What is likely wrong?

The most common causes are a failed capacitor, low refrigerant, a dirty condenser coil, or a tripped breaker. Some of these are inexpensive fixes. A failed capacitor, for example, is typically a $150–$250 repair. We will diagnose the actual cause before quoting anything.

What brands do you service and install?

We service all major brands including American Standard, Trane, Carrier, Goodman, Lennox, Rheem, and Daikin. For new installations we work primarily with American Standard and Goodman, which offer the best combination of reliability and value for North Texas homes.
